shortDescription: Adds custom drops to mobs based on configuration
oneLiner: Gives any mob extra drops on death on top of its normal loot, configured as one line per drop - by default a wither skeleton drops its skull 12.5% of the time, a golden apple 40% and netherite scrap 10%, and a warden always drops 1-3 enchanted golden apples.

configKeys.effect: List of additional mob drops. Format: mob_id;item_id;chance[;max_drops] - Example: minecraft:wither_skeleton;minecraft:wither_skeleton_skull;0.5;2

notes:
HISTORY: the module sat in the source tree unregistered from v0.12.0 until it was wired into the bundle and given a standalone jar. Anything written before that which calls it dead code (older AGENTS.md revisions, the build.gradle comment) is out of date.

LIVE SINCE v1.0.0-beta.87. `MobDropsModule` is registered in the bundle at `VanillaPlusAdditions.java:156` (`moduleManager.registerModule(new MobDropsModule());`, one of 48 registerModule calls) and ships as a standalone jar: `mob_drops` is in build.gradle's `standaloneModules` list (build.gradle:451) with the entrypoint `standalone/mob_drops/MobDropsStandalone.java`. Before that it sat in the source tree unregistered from v0.12.0 on - instantiated nowhere, so `ModulesConfig` never wrote a `[modules.mob_drops]` section, `onInitialize()` never ran and none of the four default drop rules fired. Any text that still calls the module dead code describes the pre-beta.87 state.

REGRESSION IT LEFT BEHIND. CHANGELOG.md:1288 (release 0.12.0) introduces the module ("MobDropsModule: Eigenstaendiges, konfigurierbares Modul fuer zusaetzliche Mob-Drops eingefuehrt") and CHANGELOG.md:1296 states "WitherSkeletonModule: Zusaetzliche Drop-Logik entfernt; Drop-Konfiguration in das neue mob_drops-Modul verschoben." Today `modules/wither_skeleton/` holds only `WitherSkeletonModule.java` + `config/WitherSkeletonConfig.java` and contains no `LivingDropsEvent` handler at all (the only LivingDropsEvent subscribers in the repo are mob_drops, cat_guardian, flying_fish, axolotl_guardian). Since the mob_drops target was never registered, the wither-skeleton skull/golden-apple/netherite-scrap drops have been silently missing since v0.12.0. WitherSkeletonModule is now purely a Nether skeleton-spawn blocker ("Wither Skeleton Enforcer").

DEAD NULL CHECK / SILENT PIG FALLBACK. MobDropsModule.java uses `BuiltInRegistries.ENTITY_TYPE.get(mobRl)` and then tests `if (mobType == null)`. Verified against the decompiled 1.21.1 sources: `BuiltInRegistries.ENTITY_TYPE` is a `DefaultedRegistry` with default key "pig" (BuiltInRegistries.java:141-143) and `DefaultedMappedRegistry.get(ResourceLocation)` is `@Nonnull`, returning `this.defaultValue.value()` instead of null. So the null branch is unreachable and a typo'd/unknown mob id silently attaches the drop rule to `minecraft:pig`. The item lookup is done right by accident: `BuiltInRegistries.ITEM` is likewise defaulted, to "air" (BuiltInRegistries.java:144), so `item == Items.AIR` does catch bad item ids - at the price that a deliberate `minecraft:air` drop is silently skipped too. Sibling module MobGlowModule guards correctly with `ENTITY_TYPE.containsKey(...)` before `get(...)` - mob_drops does not.

EVENT IS NOT GATED BY doMobLoot. In the patched `LivingEntity.dropAllDeathLoot` (LivingEntity.java:1461-1475), `CommonHooks.onLivingDrops(...)` is fired *after* the `if (shouldDropLoot() && gamerules.getBoolean(RULE_DOMOBLOOT))` block, so `LivingDropsEvent` fires on every server-side LivingEntity death. Extra drops from this module would therefore also appear with `doMobLoot false`. `Player` does not override `dropAllDeathLoot` - `Player.die` (Player.java:666-672) calls the inherited one for any non-spectator on a ServerLevel - so a `minecraft:player;...` rule would work as well.

max_drops SEMANTICS. `amount = maxDrops > 1 ? random.nextInt(maxDrops) + 1 : 1` -> a uniform 1..max_drops, not a fixed stack. The warden default `...;1;3` therefore means "always drops, 1-3 apples" (`nextFloat() < 1.0f` is always true, since nextFloat returns [0,1)). `DropInfo`'s explicit canonical constructor clamps `maxDrops` with `Math.max(1, maxDrops)`, so 0/negative values degrade to 1. Each rule for a mob is rolled independently; the same mob+item may be listed several times and each line rolls separately (no dedup, no merging).

CONFIG VALIDATION vs. PARSING (two different code paths, different strictness). The spec validator in MobDropsConfig (buildModuleSpecificConfig, lines 40-62) rejects entries with fewer than 3 or more than 4 `;`-parts, a `chance` outside 0.0-1.0, or a non-numeric `max_drops` (rejected entries are dropped by NeoForge's ModConfigSpec, falling back to the default list). The runtime parser in `reloadMobDropsCache()` is looser: it accepts `parts.length >= 3`, ignores parts beyond index 3, applies no range check to `chance`, and only warns on an unparsable `max_drops` (keeping 1). A `chance` of `0.0` passes validation and simply never fires (`nextFloat() < 0.0f`), with no warning. Malformed entries log a warning/error and are skipped - never fatal. The "new list element" supplier default is `"minecraft:wither_skeleton;minecraft:wither_skeleton_skull;0.5;1"`.

CACHE LIFECYCLE. `reloadMobDropsCache()` is called from `onCommonSetup()` and from `MobDropsConfig.onConfigLoad()`. It clears the cache and returns immediately when `isModuleEnabled()` is false, so a module disabled at load keeps an empty cache until the next config load. The per-drop `isModuleEnabled()` check in `onEntityDrop` is the real gate - note that AbstractModule.initialize() (AbstractModule.java:90-105) registers handlers based on `shouldInitialize()` (default `true`, AbstractModule.java:112-114, not tied to the config flag), not on the enabled flag.

SIDE. Server. Only `LivingDropsEvent` (fired from `LivingEntity.die` on a `ServerLevel`); no rendering, no keybinds, no `Minecraft.getInstance()`, no `Dist.CLIENT`/`@OnlyIn`/client package references, no network packets - a grep over the module directory for DeferredRegister, RegisterCommandsEvent, KeyMapping, ModList.isLoaded, Dist., @OnlyIn and Minecraft.getInstance returns nothing at all.

NOTHING ELSE SHIPPED. No lang keys (`en_us.json` contains no `mob_drops`/`mobdrops`/`Mob Drops` entry), no mixins (no `mixin/mob_drops/` package, nothing in `vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json`), no commands, no items/blocks/entities (no DeferredRegister in the module at all), no data/resource files (`find src/main/resources -iname '*mob_drop*'` is empty), no recipes. `enabledByDefault` comes from the interface default `Module.isEnabledByDefault()` -> true (Module.java:73-75); MobDropsModule overrides neither it nor `shouldInitialize()`. The base config adds only `enabled` (AbstractModuleConfig.java:59-60) and `debug_logging` (lines 63-66), which are not listed as module config keys by convention.

README. The only mention is README.md:306, a documentation link `- [Mob Drops](docs/mob_drops.md)`. There is no feature paragraph for the module. That link is stale in the current working tree: docs were moved to `docs/modules/mob_drops.md` (staged rename), so the whole module-doc list at README.md lines 296-309 points at old paths, while the guide links just above (lines 293-295) and at 204-206 were already updated to `docs/guides/` and `docs/modules/`.
